ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large triangle, and all 18 black dots are located on the three sides of the triangle. Counting on each side, there are 7 points (including the two endpoints of that side); the three vertices are respectively shared by two adjacent sides, so the total number of points is 7+7+7-3=18. Then reason: Choosing any 3 points usually can form a triangle, and there are C(18,3)=816 ways to choose in total. The cases that cannot form a triangle are when 3 points are collinear; in the figure, collinear triples of points occur only on the three sides of the large triangle. Each side has 7 points, and the degenerate cases of choosing 3 points from the same side are C(7,3)=35, so the three sides have 3×35=105 cases in total. Therefore the number of triangles that can be drawn is 816-105=711.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the 18 points lie on the three sides of a large triangle, with 7 points on each side when including the two endpoints of that side; the three corner points are shared between pairs of sides, giving 7+7+7-3=18 distinct points. Then count all possible triples of points, since any non-collinear triple forms a triangle: C(18,3). Subtract the degenerate triples where all three chosen points lie on one straight side of the large triangle. Each side contributes C(7,3) collinear triples, and there are 3 sides, so the count is C(18,3)-3C(7,3)=816-105=711.
